# DSL003: deprecated-directive-spelling

> Generated: do not edit this page. Regenerate with `cargo dev gen rules`.

| since | 2.0.0 |

A directive uses a deprecated `frob:` claim spelling that D120 moved or dropped.

`frob:effects`, `core`, `shell`, `calls`, `pure` and `honest` became `grimble:` verbs;
`dispatcher`, `hook`, `trusted` and `idempotent` were dropped in favour of an `accept`
exception, inference or a bound test. Old spellings parse for one minor release; apply the
attached fix (`grimble:effects none`, or an `accept` exception to complete) to migrate.

## Examples

### DSL003 deprecated directive spelling / Rust: frob:pure moved to grimble:effects none #1 (line 6) (fire)

```rust
/* frob:pure */ // warn: DSL003
fn a() {}
```

### DSL003 deprecated directive spelling / Rust: frob:dispatcher dropped for an accept exception #2 (line 13) (fire)

```rust

```

### DSL003 deprecated directive spelling / Rust: frob:effects renamed #3 (line 20) (fire)
